channel.title: Bentonville Daily
channel.description: Public records and local institutions, daily.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 27, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville School District reports 1,204 students, or 6% of its enrollment, are exempt from vaccinations this school year.
Bentonville School District reports 6% vaccine exemption rate. Data from the Arkansas Department of Education shows that 1,204 students in the Bentonville School District are exempt from vaccinations this school year, representing about 6% of total district enrollment. Officials state that exemption rates topping 5% in some Northwest Arkansas school districts threaten herd immunity.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 827 NW 8th Street. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 827 NW 8th Street from T4.1 Neighborhood General to T3.1 Neighborhood Edge within the Walkable Neighborhood Place Type.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Utility board to award a $934,988.00 contract for sanitary sewer improvements. This proposed contract with Humbard Contracting Inc. would fund repairs to sewer infrastructure in areas identified in the 2024 Sewer Capacity Study, as part of an ongoing strategy to reduce inflow and infiltration into the sewer system.
On the Bentonville Special - Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its membership, chairperson, and quorum. This item is for informational purposes, outlining how the committee is structured and operates.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to discuss the 2027 general budget. This discussion would involve the Finance Director and City Department Heads presenting their proposed budgets for the upcoming year, which would determine how city funds are allocated for services and projects.
Rogers hosts 19th annual Turkey Trot for heroes. The 19th annual Turkey Trot for Heroes took place on Thanksgiving morning in Rogers. The event honored fallen heroes and raised money for military members, veterans, and first responders through Sheep Dog Impact Assistance.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 26, 2026
item.description:
Benton County Water District #1 has lifted a boil water order for parts of Benton County east of U.S. 62.
Benton County Water District #1 lifts boil water order. A boil water order issued Tuesday for most of Benton County Water District #1's system east of U.S. 62 has been lifted.
Lowell city council approves ordinance to remove Flock cameras. Lowell's Flock cameras must be deactivated by mid-December and removed from city property by mid-January, following a new ordinance approved by the City Council.
Lowell mayor-elect reviews city job positions. Lowell's mayor-elect announced that all city job positions are undergoing review, with current employees asked to reapply alongside new applicants.
On the Bentonville Special - Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its membership, chairperson, and quorum. This item is for informational purposes and would clarify how the committee is structured and operates, including who serves on it and how many members are needed for official decisions.
Rogers seeks public input on walking and biking improvements. The City of Rogers is asking residents to provide input on plans to improve walking, biking, and other forms of active transportation throughout the community.
J.B. Hunt asks board to deny union pacific and norfolk southern merger. J.B. Hunt has requested that the board deny the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern.
Walmart becomes exclusive seller of Hi Peach Layne hair repair oil. Walmart is now the exclusive seller of hair repair oil made by Little Rock-based Hi Peach Layne, with the product released in over 1,000 locations in October.
Tyson Foods donates 14,000 pounds of nuggets to Northwest Arkansas Food Bank. Tyson Foods has made a donation of 14,000 pounds of chicken nuggets to the Northwest Arkansas Food Bank.
Proposal to lower Gravette mayor's retirement age sees pushback. Proposals to allow outgoing Gravette Mayor Kurt Maddox to keep his city-issued laptop and retire at 57 years old have received pushback from some city residents.
Walmart to be closed on Thanksgiving Day for seventh consecutive year. Walmart will be closed on Thanksgiving Day for the seventh consecutive year.
Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette asks nonprofits for wish lists. The Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette is asking area nonprofits to share their Christmas or holiday wish lists, including needs for volunteers, supplies, or gift cards.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 25, 2026
item.description:
The Fayetteville City Council will consider a resolution next week to reduce the city administration's authority over staffing and budgetary changes.
Fayetteville council to consider resolution on city administration authority. The Fayetteville City Council will consider a resolution next week that would reduce the city administration's authority and give the council more oversight on city staffing changes and budgetary amendments.
On the Bentonville Special - Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its membership, chairperson, and quorum requirements. This discussion would clarify how the committee is structured and how many members are needed for official decisions.
Boil order issued for parts of Benton County. A boil order has been issued for portions of Benton County following a water main break early Tuesday morning.
Gentry City Council approves $5.3 million in bonds for wastewater upgrades. The Gentry City Council approved nearly $5.3 million in revenue bonds to finance wastewater system upgrades.
America's Car-Mart finds buyer and files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Rogers-based America's Car-Mart has found a buyer, Cardinal Asset Holdings LLC, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization.
Construction on Bella Vista Town Center project could finish by year's end. An ongoing construction project at 400 Town Center in Bella Vista could be finished as early as the end of this year.
Pea Ridge North Davis Street sidewalk work expected to finish early. Construction on the North Davis Street sidewalk in Pea Ridge is progressing well and is expected to be completed before its deadline, according to city construction project manager Logan Johnson.
Rogers City Council member barney hayes passes away. Rogers City Council member and longtime public servant Barney Hayes has died, according to Mayor Greg Hines.
Northwest Arkansas Food Bank appoints Sabrina Thiede as COO. The Lowell-based Northwest Arkansas Food Bank has promoted Sabrina Thiede, director of programs, to vice president and chief operating officer.
Blue Crane develops over $60 million in downtown Springdale projects. Bentonville company Blue Crane is working on new commercial real estate developments in downtown Springdale, with over $60 million in projects underway as part of revitalization efforts.
Botanical Garden of the Ozarks launches two new funds totaling $150,000. The Botanical Garden of the Ozarks in Fayetteville established an endowment and a capital reserve fund totaling $150,000, marking its first endowment to support the organization.
Rogers gym hosts Thanksgiving break kids camp. A Northwest Arkansas gym in Rogers is hosting a camp during Thanksgiving break for children.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 22, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will kick off its Holiday Window Contest and Lighting of the Square on Saturday.
Bentonville to host holiday window contest and lighting of the Square. Bentonville will kick off its Holiday Window Contest and Lighting of the Square on Saturday. The Bentonville Square will light up at 6 p.m. to mark the start of the holiday season.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 608 NW B Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the zoning classification of the property at 608 NW B Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve contract for Riordan Road/US 71 intersection improvements. This resolution would authorize a contract with Garver, LLC for $69,395.00 to provide professional engineering services for improvements at the Riordan Road/US 71 intersection.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Committee to authorize additional funds for Airport Hangar Access Road Project. This resolution would authorize an additional $2,983.72 for the Airport Hangar Access Road Project to cover the cost of additional materials testing.
Pea Ridge Public Library collects food for fines program. The Pea Ridge Public Library is collecting food donations through the end of November. The annual Food for Fines program allows individuals to exchange food donations for past-due library fines.
Maysville Volunteer Fire Department hosts annual chili supper and auction. The Maysville Volunteer Fire Department, serving parts of rural Benton County, hosted its annual Chili supper and auction on Saturday. The event encouraged community members from across Northwest Arkansas to gather.
Museum of native american history features tennessee artist's work. A Tennessee artist is bringing her work to the Museum of Native American History in Bentonville. The exhibit includes "The Resting Warrior," an image from the spiritual world of the Mississippian Mound Builders.
Northwest Arkansas philanthropists recognized at luncheon. The Northwest Arkansas chapter of the Association of Fundraising Professionals honored area philanthropists at its National Philanthropy Day luncheon on November 4. The event, held at the Fayetteville Public Library, also marked the organization's silver jubilee.
Bella Vista Community Church announces advent service and food pantry collections. Bella Vista Community Church, located at 75 E. Lancashire Blvd., has announced an Advent service. The church is also requesting food pantry collections for Thanksgiving.
Arkansas freshman quarterback hank Hendrix makes college debut. Seventeen-year-old freshman quarterback Hank Hendrix made his college debut for Arkansas in a loss to Texas. Hendrix is an early enrollee who skipped his final year at Fayetteville High School.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 21, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville City Council and Finance Committee will consider multiple proposals, including a rezoning request and a planned unit development, at meetings this week.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 608 NW B Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed rezoning would change the zoning classification of the property at 608 NW B Street, potentially allowing for different types of development than currently permitted for suburban single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Committee to authorize additional funds for Airport Hangar Access Road Project. This resolution would authorize an additional $2,983.72 for the Airport Hangar Access Road Project to cover the cost of additional materials testing.
Regional wastewater study recommends new collaborative for infrastructure. A draft state-commissioned study on regional wastewater recommends a new collaborative to coordinate infrastructure planning and funding. The study indicates that Northwest Arkansas has enough wastewater treatment capacity for tens of thousands more residents, but it is not located where the region is growing.
Rogers townhomes sell for $22 million. An 86-unit multifamily development located along Interstate 49 in Rogers recently sold for $22 million. The purchase price for the two-story development equates to $255,813 per unit.
Harps Food Stores promotes Debbie Creek to chief financial officer. Springdale-based grocer Harps Food Stores promoted Debbie Creek, previously vice president of finance, to chief financial officer. This was one of three promotions announced by the company on Friday.
Tyson Foods updates board of directors. Tyson Foods announced updates to its board of directors.
7 brew coffee chain featured on forbes' 'America's favorite restaurants' list. Northwest Arkansas-based coffee chain 7 Brew was included on Forbes' 'America's Favorite Restaurants' list. This recognition is based on a survey of over 100,000 people.
Pea Ridge to resume December Horse Carriage Rides. Downtown Pea Ridge will bring back its Horse Carriage Rides in December. A new system will be implemented this year to facilitate easier rides.
Northwest Arkansas commercial real estate demand remains strong. Demand for commercial real estate space in Northwest Arkansas increased during the third quarter, despite high land and construction costs. A report from Colliers Arkansas noted tight retail space, rising office rents, and constrained land for industrial locations.
Fayetteville and NWA Continuum seek partners for cold weather shelters. Fayetteville and the Northwest Arkansas Continuum of Care are seeking more organizations and volunteers to help operate cold weather shelters. This effort comes as one of the first hard freezes of the season is anticipated this weekend.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 20, 2026
item.description:
The Washington County Quorum Court approved a 12-month moratorium on the construction and development of data centers.
Washington County Quorum Court approves 12-month data center moratorium. The Washington County Quorum Court on Thursday passed a yearlong moratorium on the construction and development of data centers in the county.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider new rules for short-term rentals. This ordinance would amend the city's zoning code to add specific regulations regarding the density and use of short-term rentals in Bella Vista.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve contract for Riordan Road/US 71 intersection improvements. The Mayor and City Clerk are asked to enter into a $69,395.00 contract with Garver, LLC for professional engineering services related to the Riordan Road/US 71 intersection improvement project.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider requiring approval for license plate readers and facial recognition systems. This ordinance would prohibit the City of Bella Vista from acquiring or activating an automatic license plate reader system or facial recognition and identification system without prior approval from the City Council.
Rogers City Council meeting cancelled due to Thanksgiving holiday. The Rogers City Council meeting scheduled for November 24 has been cancelled due to the Thanksgiving Holiday.
Single Parent Scholarship Fund of Northwest Arkansas breaks ground on Springdale headquarters. Bentonville-based nonprofit Single Parent Scholarship Fund of Northwest Arkansas broke ground Thursday on a 13,000-square-foot headquarters in Springdale. The project is part of the nonprofit’s $7.4 million fundraising effort and is expected to be completed in 2028.
Antique Brick & Block opens Springdale store with $8 million investment. Antique Brick & Block, a Little Rock-based manufacturer and distributor, is investing about $8 million in its new Springdale location and adding staff.
Walmart reports $4.95 billion third-quarter profit. Walmart posted a fiscal third-quarter profit of $4.95 billion, or 62 cents per share, down from $6.14 billion, or 77 cents per share, a year ago.
Walmart quarterly net income down 19.5%, revenue up 5.2%. Walmart posted third-quarter net income of $4.945 billion, down 19.5% from a year ago. Earnings per share before one-time adjustments totaled 62 cents.
Walmart raises outlook for the year for the third time. Walmart reported solid third-quarter sales gains and raised its outlook for the year for the third time.
Regional planning committee recommends new framework for transportation projects. Northwest Arkansas transportation officials are recommending changes to how regional transportation projects are evaluated and prioritized.
Fayetteville School Board discusses legislative priorities and future bond issuances. Fayetteville School District officials are prioritizing early childhood education as the next legislative session approaches, and discussed proposed future bond issuances.
Daniel Barnes takes on new role as central regional executive. Daniel Barnes, former president of the Fayetteville branch of McClelland Consulting Engineers (MCE), has taken on a new role as central regional executive.
Ozark united FC founders discuss team future at virtual town hall. The founders of a professional soccer franchise planned for Northwest Arkansas are working to get the club off the ground.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 19, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will offer free parking and shuttle services for its annual Lighting of the Square celebration.
Bentonville offers free parking and shuttle for Lighting of the Square. The city of Bentonville will provide free parking and shuttle services for its annual Lighting of the Square celebration.
Benton county Planning board approves school and drone facility plans. The Benton County Planning Board approved site plans for a new elementary school for the Siloam Springs School District and a drone facility.
Bentonville School Board votes to phase out R.E. Baker elementary. The Bentonville School District School Board voted to phase out R.E. Baker Elementary School, with kindergarten enrollment ending.
Rogers Public schools to implement block scheduling in 2027-28. Rogers Public Schools plans to implement block scheduling beginning in the fall of 2027 for the 2027-28 school year.
Fayetteville to close section of Old Wire Road next week. A section of Old Wire Road in Fayetteville will close next week for infrastructure work.
Bentonville Square property and parking sell for $13.54 million. A 38,410-square-foot office building and its 38,264-square-foot parking garage on the Bentonville Square recently sold in separate transactions totaling $13.54 million.
Fayetteville receives four new Opportunity Zone designations. The U.S. Department of the Treasury approved four new Opportunity Zones in Fayetteville, following a state recommendation.
Governor Sanders announces $261 million for water infrastructure. Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders announced over $261 million in additional financial assistance for 75 water and wastewater projects, benefiting more than 740,000 Arkansans, including those in Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley.
NWACC recognized as bronze-level Bicycle Friendly University. NorthWest Arkansas Community College (NWACC) was recognized as a Bronze-level Bicycle Friendly University by the League of American Bicyclists.
Kiefer Sage hires Kevin Wisel as chief financial and administrative officer. Rogers-based manufacturer Kiefer Sage named Kevin Wisel as its new chief financial and administrative officer, a new role for the company.
Calara Group promotes Don Draper to president. Calara Group, the land development arm of Fayetteville-based Rausch Companies, named Don Draper as its president.
On the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Committee agenda: Committee to discuss 2026 expenditures. The committee would review and discuss its spending plans for the upcoming year.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 18, 2026
item.description:
A portion of Northeast Blueberry Lane in Bentonville will close Wednesday for utility construction.
Northeast Blueberry Lane to close for utility work. A section of Northeast Blueberry Lane in Bentonville will be closed Wednesday for the construction of a new utility crossing.
Bentonville school board votes to phase out R.E. Baker elementary. The Bentonville School Board has voted to close R.E. Baker Elementary in phases, with current kindergarteners being the last class to attend.
Fayetteville City Council approves $165,000 for 7hills Homeless Center. The Fayetteville City Council approved $165,000 to help the 7hills Homeless Center remain open. This funding is intended to keep the nonprofit operational through the end of the year.
Bentonville to begin annual fall leaf collection in December. The city of Bentonville will start its annual fall leaf curbside pickup program next month.
Pat Walker Center for Success to break ground in springdale. The Single Parent Scholarship Fund of Northwest Arkansas will begin construction on its permanent home, the Pat Walker Center for Success, on Thursday.
Fayetteville to dedicate historical marker for henderson school. The City of Fayetteville will recognize Henderson School, the city's first public school for Black students, with a new historical marker this Saturday.
Walmart to release third quarter results Thursday. Walmart is scheduled to release its third quarter financial results on Thursday morning.
Bentonville office complex sells for $30.75 million. A seven-building office complex totaling approximately 138,000 square feet in Bentonville recently sold for $30.75 million.
Rogers board approves variances for Life Time athletic club. A 27-acre mixed-use development in Rogers' Pinnacle Hills area moved closer to construction after variance requests were approved for a planned Life Time athletic club.
J.B. Hunt subsidiary co-designs new technology platform. Nashville-based startup Groundtruth launched its invoice validation platform, which was developed and co-designed with a subsidiary of Lowell-based J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc.
Sage Partners brokers $5.4 million in property sales. Commercial real estate firm Cushman & Wakefield / Sage Partners recently brokered $5.4 million in property sales near the University of Arkansas.
Kara Armas sworn in as Arkansas House District 8 member. Pea Ridge Republican Kara Armas was sworn in as a state representative for Arkansas House District 8, filling a vacant seat for eight weeks.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 17, 2026
item.description:
The Lowell Planning Commission approved conditional use permits for two small businesses after discussions.
Lowell Planning Commission approves conditional use permits for two businesses. The Lowell Planning Commission approved two conditional use permits for small businesses on Monday, following discussions regarding several concerns.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 608 NW B Street from single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development than suburban single-family homes at 608 NW B Street, moving towards a more mixed-use neighborhood style.
On the Bentonville Schools Board of Education agenda: Board to convene its meeting. This item is for the formal start of the meeting, including a welcome, call to order, and roll call of board members.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to waive competitive bids for 750 copper underground wire for the Tiger Overpass. This ordinance would allow the Utility Board to purchase 750 copper underground wire from Stuart Irby without competitive bidding, due to market volatility and lead times for these products.
Fayetteville Advertising and Promotion Commission fires CEO Ryan Hauck. The Fayetteville Advertising and Promotion Commission voted Monday to fire Experience Fayetteville CEO Ryan Hauck. Experience Fayetteville is the agency that manages the city’s tourism marketing efforts.
Tyson Foods reports $74 million quarterly loss. Springdale-based Tyson Foods Inc. reported a $74 million loss in its fiscal fourth quarter. The loss was attributed to costs from plant closures and legal settlements, though the company indicated that issues in the beef segment might be improving.
Fayetteville council to consider funding for 7hills homeless services. The Fayetteville council will consider approving funding to help 7hills homeless services remain open. The Fayetteville nonprofit is facing an uncertain future.
Siloam Springs School District to give $150 holiday bonuses to some substitute staff. Some substitute staff in the Siloam Springs School District will receive a one-time $150 holiday bonus. The bonus will be included in their paychecks this Friday, coinciding with National Substitute Educators Day.
Ozark united FC to host town hall meeting. Ozark United FC, a planned professional soccer club in Northwest Arkansas, is hosting a town hall. The team has not yet begun playing or constructed a stadium, and the timeline remains uncertain.
Ozark Society Sugar Creek Chapter to host invasive plant pull. The Ozark Society Sugar Creek Chapter will host an invasive plant pull at Logan Springs Preserve, 15300 Osage Hill Road, near Siloam Springs. The event is scheduled from 9:30 a.m. to noon on Thursday.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 16, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will restrict high-powered e-bikes on its trails, joining other Arkansas cities with similar regulations.
Bentonville restricts high-powered e-bikes on trails. New regulations in Bentonville will target powerful electric motorcycles, aligning with rules established by other Arkansas communities for electric bicycles.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 608 NW B Street from single-family to neighborhood edge.. This proposed change would allow for a different type of housing development, moving from suburban single-family to a neighborhood edge designation within the Traditional Neighborhood place type.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to waive competitive bids for 750 copper underground wire for the Tiger Overpass. This ordinance would allow the purchase of 750 copper underground wire from Stuart Irby without competitive bidding, due to market volatility and lead times for these products.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider requiring approval for license plate readers and facial recognition systems. This ordinance would prohibit the City of Bella Vista from acquiring or activating an automatic license plate reader system or facial recognition and identification system without prior approval from the City Council.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport board reviews strategic plan. Northwest Arkansas National Airport officials have achieved most benchmarks from their 2019 strategic plan, doubling nonstop destinations and reducing debt as they prepare for future regional growth.
Flights temporarily halted at XNA and nationwide. Flights were halted at the Northwest Arkansas National Airport and across the United States on Friday due to "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," according to the FAA.
La Prensa Libre AR to close in December. La Prensa Libre AR, the only all-Spanish print newspaper in a wide regional area, will cease circulation on December 28, with its final edition publishing on December 30.
Northwest Arkansas Community College dedicates EMS lab. Northwest Arkansas Community College dedicated its EMS lab to Jamin Snarr, its former EMS director, for his 30 years of service.
Centric expands into Northwest Arkansas. Centric has expanded its operations into the Northwest Arkansas region.
United Bank hires Joe Weinsinger as vice president. United Bank has hired Joe Weinsinger as vice president, commercial lender.
Little Flock donates building to Pea Ridge police Department. The city of Little Flock donated a double-wide manufactured building to the Pea Ridge Police Department, significantly increasing their office space.
Fayetteville park to close temporarily for bridge installation. Parts of a park in northern Fayetteville will close next week for the installation of a new feature.
Fayetteville offers overnight shelter due to dropping temperatures. The City of Fayetteville activated its extreme weather response on Sunday, November 15, to provide residents with access to warm shelter as overnight temperatures were expected to drop.
7hills Homeless Center postpones move to new shelter. 7hills Homeless Center has postponed its plans to relocate its Day Center shelter after recent funding cuts.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 4, 2026
item.description:
Rogers voters approved a $457.25 million bond issue to fund projects for streets, parks, public safety, and animal services, and extended a 1-cent sales tax.
Rogers voters approve $457.25 million bond issue and sales tax extension. Rogers residents voted to approve all six items in a $457.25 million bond issue for streets, parks and recreation, public safety, and animal services projects. Voters also extended an existing 1% sales tax to enable the bond issue.
Bentonville City Council incumbents retain seats in election. Incumbent members of the Bentonville City Council were reelected in Tuesday's election.
Democrats claim four seats on Benton County Quorum Court. Democrats won four seats on the Benton County Quorum Court on Tuesday, altering the body's previous all-Republican composition.
Wendy Henson elected Centerton mayor. Wendy Henson defeated Cliff Thompson to become Centerton's next mayor in Tuesday's election.
Bill Adams elected Lowell mayor. Former City Councilman Bill Adams will be the new mayor of Lowell after defeating two-term incumbent Chris Moore in Tuesday's election.
Delta Air Lines to offer daily nonstop flights between austin and Northwest Arkansas. Delta Air Lines will begin offering daily nonstop flights connecting Austin-Bergstrom International Airport and Northwest Arkansas National Airport in March 2027.
On the Bentonville Library Advisory Board agenda: Bentonville students to submit artwork for 'America 250' celebration. The City of Bentonville invited students in 7th through 12th grade to create two-dimensional artwork illustrating what they love about America, in celebration of the country’s 250th anniversary.
Fayetteville City Council race to continue to runoff. One Fayetteville City Council seat will proceed to a runoff election following a close race on Tuesday.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 3, 2026
item.description:
Rogers voters will decide on Tuesday whether to authorize up to $457.25 million across six bond questions for streets, parks, fire and police facilities, animal services, and refinancing existing debt.
Rogers voters to consider $457.25 million bond issue. On Tuesday, November 3, Rogers voters will decide on a bond issue totaling up to $457.25 million. The funds would address needs for streets, parks, fire and police facilities, animal services, and refinancing existing debt.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to approve a lot split at 607 SE C Street. This would divide Lot 13, Block F of Orchard Addition at 607 SE C Street into separate parcels.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider a fence setback waiver at 337 NW A Street and an amendment to a large scale development at 3110 SE J Street. The first waiver would allow a fence at 337 NW A Street to be placed differently than city code typically allows. The second item would amend the phasing plan for the J Street of Bentonville Large Scale Development at 3110 SE J Street.
Centerton mayoral candidates make final push before Election Day. Centerton will elect a new mayor for the first time in 16 years, with Wendy Henson and Cliff Thompson as the two candidates.
Benton and Washington counties report early voting turnout. After more than two weeks of early voting, Northwest Arkansas residents showed a higher turnout rate than during the previous midterms.
Voting locations open for 2026 General Election. Voting for the 2026 General Election is on Tuesday, November 3, with locations open across Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley.
America's Car-Mart lenders extend loan relief. Rogers-based America's Car-Mart's lenders approved a $5 million loan last month and have extended loan relief again.
Postal Service moves mail sorting from Fayetteville to Oklahoma City. The U.S. Postal Service moved mail sorting from Fayetteville to Oklahoma City and Tulsa in September, according to the president of the local postal workers union.
Nonstop flights between XNA and Austin to resume in March. Nonstop flights between Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) in Benton County and Austin, Texas, will return in March 2027 after a six-year hiatus.
Solar array completed for Beaver Water District. Madison Energy Infrastructure and Verogy completed an approximately $10 million solar array for Lowell-based utility Beaver Water District.
Bella Vista Fly Tyers to hold gear sale. Bella Vista Fly Tyers will hold their annual sale of used fishing and outdoor gear from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. Friday and Saturday. The sale will take place at United Lutheran Church, 100 Cooper Road in Bella Vista.
Nonprofits prepare for Fayetteville veterans Day Parade. Nonprofits across Northwest Arkansas are preparing for Fayetteville's second annual Veteran's Day Parade, an event to honor veterans.
Waste management service offers campaign sign recycling. A waste management service for Washington and Madison counties is reminding residents that campaign yard signs can be recycled at its facilities.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 2, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville is undertaking a two-year project to improve the Rainbow Curve intersection and alleviate traffic congestion.
Bentonville begins two-year rainbow curve intersection improvements. Work has started on a two-year project in Bentonville to reduce traffic congestion and improve safety at a major intersection on the south side of town.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to approve a lot split at 607 SE C Street. This would divide Lot 13, Block F of Orchard Addition at 607 SE C Street into separate parcels.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider a fence setback waiver at 337 NW A Street and an amendment to the J Street Phasing Plan at 3110 SE J Street. This would allow a fence at 337 NW A Street to be placed differently than specified in Section 50-510(e)(1) and would amend the phasing plan for the J Street of Bentonville Large Scale Development at 3110 SE J Street.
Rogers water Utilities Commission to meet November 16. The Rogers Water Utilities Commission is scheduled to meet on November 16 at 4:00 PM at 601 S. 2nd Street.
Planners hope to extend Razorback Greenway to Missouri line. With the 41st mile of the Razorback Greenway officially open in Bella Vista, planners are now focusing on extending the trail to the Missouri state line.
Fayetteville celebrates opening of Underwood Park. Fayetteville held a ribbon-cutting celebration for its newest park, Underwood Park, on Sunday, November 1. The park offers paths for walking and biking, and spaces for community gathering.
Fayetteville's Underwood Park officially opens. Underwood Park in Fayetteville officially opened on Sunday, November 1, providing residents with a new outdoor space.
Fayetteville hosts fifth annual Día de los Muertos celebration. The Community Creative Center in Fayetteville hosted its fifth annual Día de los Muertos celebration on Sunday, featuring art, live music, and Mexican traditions.
NWA Makers Market draws hundreds of vendors and shoppers. The NWA Makers Market at the Washington County Fairgrounds in Fayetteville hosted hundreds of local vendors for shoppers on Sunday.
Arkansas voters to decide on taxes and city governance on November 3. Voters across Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley will decide on November 3 how communities will fund roads, water systems, public safety, and local government.
Local students craft special stickers for Washington County voters. Two local students in Fayetteville have hand-crafted special 'I Voted' stickers that will be given to voters in Washington County on Election Day.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — November 1, 2026
item.description:
Northwest Arkansas National Airport will add daily nonstop flights to Austin, Texas, starting next year.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport announces daily nonstop flights to Austin. The Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) announced it will add daily nonstop flights to Austin, Texas, starting next year.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider a lot split at 607 SE C Street. This item proposes splitting Lot 13, Block F of Orchard Addition at 607 SE C Street, which could create new parcels of land.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider a fence setback waiver at 337 NW A Street and an amendment to a large scale development at 3110 SE J Street. The Commission would consider a waiver for fence and wall setbacks at 337 NW A Street, and an amendment to the J Street of Bentonville Phasing Plan Large Scale Development at 3110 SE J Street.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 31, 2026
item.description:
Pea Ridge city staff recommends a redesign for the Knox Trail Planned Zoning District proposal.
Pea Ridge staff recommends redesign for knox trail planned Zoning District. Pea Ridge city staff has recommended a redesign for the Knox Trail Planned Zoning District proposal. A developer is envisioning a mixed-use neighborhood that would honor historical heritage.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and election of officers. This discussion would clarify the committee's role and what matters it can consider, potentially leading to recommendations for the City Council.
Rogers City Council Committee of the Whole to hold 2027 budget session. The Rogers City Council Committee of the Whole will hold a 2027 Budget Session Meeting on November 9, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 11:59 PM at 301 W Chestnut Street.
Rogers Airport Commission reschedules meeting to November 10. The Rogers Airport Commission Meeting, originally scheduled for November 11, 2026, has been rescheduled to November 10, 2026, from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at #6 Hammerschmidt Drive.
Rogers Advertising and promotions Commission meeting moved to November 18. The Rogers Advertising and Promotions Commission Meeting has been moved to November 18, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM at 317 W Walnut, due to Veterans Day.
Northwest Arkansas early voting numbers surpass 2022 figures. Early voting in Northwest Arkansas is significantly outpacing 2022 numbers, with voters continuing to show up at the polls at a higher rate than last midterms.
Northwest Arkansas Community college offers bicycle tech program. Northwest Arkansas Community College's bicycle tech program is reshaping cycling mechanic education. The program operates in a workshop filled with rows of suspended bicycles.
Walmart AMP announces expansion to hospitality complex. The Walmart AMP, Arkansas' largest outdoor venue for concerts, will expand two existing facilities ahead of next year's concert series.
Northwest Arkansas Land Trust protects over 10,000 acres. The Northwest Arkansas Land Trust has surpassed 10,000 acres of permanently protected land. A new conservation easement near Winslow connects important wildlife habitats and preserves a scenic section of the Ozark Mountains.
Springdale Animal Services starts new donation drive for halloween. Springdale Animal Services has started a new fall tradition, leaving out trick-or-treat baskets around the shelter for visitors to fill with treats, toys, blankets, and other goodies for adoptable cats and dogs.
Elizabeth Richardson Center hosts open house in Springdale. The Elizabeth Richardson Center hosted an open house on Thursday, featuring costumes and trick-or-treating, to familiarize attendees with their program.
Benton County organization helps families celebrate Christmas. A Benton County organization is getting an early start to ensure everyone has a great Christmas.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 30, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville School Board members learned that district enrollment has topped 20,000, with school choice and housing development impacting future growth.
Bentonville district enrollment tops 20,000. Bentonville School Board members learned Tuesday that district enrollment has exceeded 20,000 students. Factors such as school choice, birth rates, and housing development will continue to influence enrollment and facilities planning.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to review proposed amendments to the Bentonville Community Code. This item involves potential changes to the city's community code, which could affect various aspects of development and land use throughout Bentonville.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and elect officers. This discussion would clarify what matters the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can consider and what recommendations it can make to the City Council.
Washington County jury reverses Fayetteville decision on Dickson Street project. A Washington County jury overturned the denial of a student housing development proposed for Dickson Street on Thursday, following a two-day trial.
Fayetteville School Board approves employee bonuses. Fayetteville School District employees will receive bonuses in their November paychecks, following a vote by the school board Thursday evening.
Fayetteville development near gulley park names first tenant. A locally-owned restaurant plans to open a new location in east Fayetteville, becoming the first tenant named for a development near Gulley Park.
Fayetteville School Board to review updated AI policy. The Fayetteville School Board will review the district's new artificial intelligence policy at its November meeting.
Fuel accelerator hosts showcase day in Bentonville. Eleven national and international startups showcased their latest artificial intelligence and machine learning technology in Northwest Arkansas on Wednesday night.
Community Blood Center of the Ozarks to host 'I Love Lucy' blood drive. The Community Blood Center of the Ozarks will host an "I Love Lucy" blood drive next week in Bentonville. The event honors Lucy Tedder, who is nearing a milestone in her leukemia treatment.
University of Arkansas researchers lead maternal health project. The Institute for Integrative and Innovative Research (I3R) at the University of Arkansas is leading a maternal health research project. This initiative is in partnership with Springdale-based healthcare provider Community Clinic.
Highlands Oncology Group works to improve cancer treatment in Northwest Arkansas. Springdale-based Highlands Oncology Group (HOG) continues to expand drug trials and experimental treatments. These efforts aim to provide more options for patients in later stages of cancer.
Companies expand and open in Northwest Arkansas and Fort Smith. Multiple companies have recently expanded, opened, or plan to do so in Northwest Arkansas and the Fort Smith metro. This includes Greenbrier-based First Service Bank, which will open a new location.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 29, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville and Bella Vista planning commissions are set to discuss rezonings and other land use proposals this week.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to review proposed amendments to the Bentonville Community Code. These proposed changes would update the rules and regulations that govern development and land use throughout the city.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to review a proposed lot split at 44 Watson Drive. This item concerns a proposal to divide the property at 44 Watson Drive into separate lots, which could change how the land is developed or used.
Marriott autograph collection hotel opens in Rogers. The first Marriott Autograph Collection Hotel in Arkansas has celebrated its grand opening in Rogers.
LISA Academy opens Fayetteville Middle-High School. LISA Academy has opened a new Middle-High School campus in Fayetteville, continuing its expansion plans in Northwest Arkansas.
Walmart, Delta Air Lines ordered to detail consumer data use by FTC. The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has ordered Walmart, Delta Air Lines, and other companies to provide detailed information on how they use consumer data for pricing.
Fayetteville properties sell for $5.4 million. Spaces in Fayetteville have been sold for a total of $5.4 million.
Archie's Sandwichery expands to Fayetteville. Archie's Sandwichery, a Bentonville sandwich shop, is expanding its operations with a new location in Fayetteville.
Northwest and central Arkansas lead statewide job growth in September. The majority of Arkansas's job gains in September came from the central Arkansas and Northwest Arkansas metro areas, accounting for 85.5% of net job gains statewide.
Walmart launches holiday meal basket for $35. Walmart has introduced a 'Holiday Meal Basket' designed to feed 10 people for $35.
Early voting turnout up in benton and washington counties. More than halfway through the early voting period, turnout in Benton and Washington counties is exceeding figures from the 2022 midterms.
Concerns raised over salem road damage from Highway 112 expansion traffic. Residents and county officials are expressing concerns about potential damage to Salem Road from dump truck traffic related to a separate excavation proposal tied to the Highway 112 widening project.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 28, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce has named Emily Medlock as its interim executive director.
Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce names interim executive director. Emily Medlock has been appointed as the interim executive director of the Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce.
Bentonville organizations to receive over $1.1 million anonymous donation. Two Bentonville entities are slated to receive more than $1.1 million from an anonymous donor.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to review proposed amendments to the Bentonville Community Code. This item involves potential changes to the city's community code, which sets the rules for development and land use across Bentonville.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to review a proposed lot split at 44 Watson Drive. This item concerns a proposal to divide the property at 44 Watson Drive, which could change the number or size of lots available at this location.
Walmart and Care Access to establish three new clinical trial centers. Walmart and clinical research organization Care Access are partnering to open three new clinical trial centers.
Crystal Bridges Museum names galleries in expansion. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville has announced the naming of several galleries and community spaces within its new 114,000-square-foot expansion, which opened in June.
WEHCO Media Inc. announces workforce reductions. WEHCO Media Inc., publisher of the Arkansas Democrat Gazette, announced it is laying off approximately 30% of its workforce, including 25% of employees at the Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, effective by year’s end. This includes 28 employees in Northwest Arkansas, with 13 from the newsroom.
Northwest Arkansas sales tax revenue remains mostly flat. Combined sales tax revenue gains in the four largest cities of Northwest Arkansas were up 0.94% for the first 10 reporting months of the year, indicating muted consumer spending.
Gravette schools celebrate academic achievements and new facilities. The Gravette School District is recognizing academic achievements, new accessible playground equipment, and the completion of a six-classroom addition at Gravette High School.
Bentonville school wins 2026 Arkansas Grown School Garden of the year. A Bentonville school was among the winners of the 2026 Arkansas Grown School Garden of the Year Contest, announced by the Arkansas Department of Agriculture in partnership with Farm Credit.
Siloam Springs water treatment plant upgraded with 2018 sales tax funds. Funds from the 2018 renewal of the Siloam Springs 5/8th-cent sales tax were utilized to upgrade the water treatment plant, correcting previous incorrect information.
Fayetteville proposes $291.9 million budget for 2027. Fayetteville's proposed 2027 budget is nearly $292 million, an increase of about $18 million from this year, with plans for more spending on personnel, infrastructure, and public transportation, alongside reductions in some operating expenses and community funding. The budget also proposes a 15% decrease to the city's library funding contribution.
Fayetteville officials to introduce ordinance targeting high-speed electric motorcycles. Mayor Molly Rawn and City Council Member Sarah Bunch will introduce an ordinance at the October 27 City Council agenda session to address safety concerns regarding electric motorcycles and high-speed electric devices in Fayetteville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 27, 2026
item.description:
The Fayetteville Planning Commission approved a preliminary plat for a 115-lot subdivision near Underwood Park.
Fayetteville Planning Commission approves 115-lot subdivision. The Fayetteville Planning Commission approved a preliminary plat for more than 100 residential lots near Underwood Park. A developer aims to bring a 115-lot subdivision to land near the park.
Siloam Springs Planning Commission reviews housing incentive program. The Siloam Springs Planning Commission is reviewing a city program that would offer incentives to developers for constructing needed housing.
Bentonville area chamber of commerce names emily medlock interim executive director. The Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce has named Emily Medlock as its interim executive director.
Walmart expands Better Care Services with General Medicine partnership. Walmart is expanding its Better Care Services platform through a new partnership with General Medicine, a digital healthcare services marketplace.
Fayetteville announces road closure on Tuesday. The city of Fayetteville announced plans to close a portion of a city roadway for most of Tuesday. A stretch of road west of the University of Arkansas will be closed during daytime hours for utility work.
Washington County Election Commission denies federal monitors in polling locations. The Washington County Election Commission unanimously denied federal election monitors from being allowed inside polling locations on Election Day.
AT&T internet outage affects nearly 400 Northwest Arkansas customers. An AT&T internet outage affected nearly 400 customers in Northwest Arkansas on Monday, leaving some without internet and streaming services into the evening.
Rogers Public Education Foundation to recognize Wall of Distinction honorees. The Rogers Public Education Foundation is set to recognize its 2027 Wall of Distinction honorees, including two district administrators and a scientist who worked on NASA spaceflight missions. The foundation will honor three individuals for their contributions to the school district and career achievements.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 501 N Main Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the classification of the property at 501 N Main Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge, which could allow for different types of development.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to accept a grant for a workforce housing infrastructure pilot program. This resolution would authorize the city to accept grant funds up to $5,000,000.00 from the Walton Family Foundation for a workforce housing infrastructure participation pilot program, with $3,000,000.00 recognized in the 2026 budget.
On the Bentonville Schools Board Work Session agenda: Board to convene for its work session. This item covers the opening formalities of the meeting, including the welcome, call to order, and roll call of board members.
Downtown Bentonville seeks vendors for first Holiday Market. Downtown Bentonville Incorporated is seeking vendors for its first-ever Holiday Market, scheduled for December.
Grammy winners Time for three to perform with Rogers high students November 10. Grammy and Emmy-winning ensemble Time for Three will return to the Walton Arts Center for a performance featuring their original music, including a new concerto, with Rogers High students on November 10.
Circles NWA offers voter planning in Bentonville and Fayetteville. Community-driven nonprofit Circles NWA is hosting two voter planning nights to help voters prepare for the upcoming Election Day.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 26, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville's City Council and Combined Committee of the Whole will meet on October 27 to consider various city matters.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 501 N Main Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the classification of the property at 501 N Main Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge, which could allow for a different type of development than single-family homes.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to accept a grant for a workforce housing infrastructure pilot program. This resolution would authorize the city to accept grant funds up to $5,000,000.00 from the Walton Family Foundation for a pilot program aimed at workforce housing infrastructure. The 2026 budget would be amended to recognize the first installment of $3,000,000.00.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve a contract for engineering services for the 2026 bond-funded radio tower project. This would authorize a contract not to exceed $250,000.00 with Horner & Shifrin for professional engineering services needed to construct the new radio tower.
On the Bentonville Schools Board Work Session agenda: Board to welcome attendees and call the meeting to order. This is a routine procedural step to begin the meeting, including the Pledge of Allegiance and roll call.
Gentry School District and city consider street project partnership. The Gentry School District and the city are considering a partnership to convert a donated driveway into a paved city street. This project would create secondary access to school campuses and upgrade municipal utilities.
Arkansas awards $2.4 million in grants for Northwest Arkansas transportation projects. The Arkansas Department of Transportation has awarded $2.4 million in grants to cities and universities in Benton and Washington counties. The funds are designated for transportation projects, including trail improvements and pedestrian infrastructure.
RJW Logistics Group to open second Northwest Arkansas office. Chicago-based RJW Logistics Group, which already has a Bentonville office, plans to open an additional Northwest Arkansas office. This expansion is due to client growth and to support demand for a new logistics program.
More than 77,000 residents cast early votes in Northwest Arkansas. Over 77,000 early votes were cast in Washington and Benton counties during the first week of early voting. Early voting began on October 19 and concluded its first week on Saturday.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 25, 2026
item.description:
Benton County may change its appeals process for planning board denials after several decisions were overturned this year.
Benton County considers altering planning appeals process. Benton County may change how developers can appeal project denials from the county Planning Board. This consideration follows several board decisions being overturned this year.
Bentonville extends partial closure of Southwest D Street. The temporary partial closure of a section of Southwest D Street in Bentonville has been extended.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 501 N Main Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 501 N Main Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge, allowing for a different type of development than single-family homes.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to accept a grant for a workforce housing infrastructure pilot program. This resolution would authorize the city to accept grant funds up to $5,000,000.00 from the Walton Family Foundation for a pilot program aimed at workforce housing infrastructure. The 2026 budget would be amended to recognize an initial $3,000,000.00 of these funds.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve a contract for engineering services for the 2026 bond-funded radio tower project. This would authorize a contract not to exceed $250,000.00 with Horner & Shifrin for professional engineering services needed to construct the new radio tower.
On the Bentonville Schools Board Work Session agenda: Board to welcome attendees and call the meeting to order. This is a routine procedural step to begin the meeting, including the Pledge of Allegiance and a roll call of board members.
Northwest Arkansas cycling industry series begins. A new series exploring two decades of cycling industry growth and its impact on Northwest Arkansas has begun.
NWA Cannabis and Wellness Expo returns to Fayetteville Town Center. The NWA Cannabis and Wellness Expo returned to Fayetteville Town Center on Saturday. The event offered educational sessions, wellness activities, and opportunities for medical marijuana certification.
Hundreds gather in Bentonville for 'More than pink' walk. Hundreds of breast cancer survivors and supporters gathered in Bentonville on Saturday morning for the 'More Than Pink' Walk.
Springdale Parks department hosts Halloween Fest Costume Contest. The Springdale Halloween Fest Costume Contest was held at Luther George Park on Saturday. Locals competed for prizes in multiple costume categories.
NWA journalists to perform Gridiron Show on October 29-30. NWA journalists will perform the Gridiron Show on October 29-30. The show includes a song commenting on public libraries and a tribute to Dolly Parton.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 24, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville, Bella Vista, and Bentonville Schools will hold public meetings this week to discuss various city and school matters.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 501 N Main Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 501 N Main Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge, which could allow for a different type of development than single-family homes.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve a contract for engineering services for the 2026 bond-funded radio tower project. This would authorize a contract not to exceed $250,000.00 with Horner & Shifrin for professional engineering services needed to construct the new radio tower.
On the Bentonville Schools Board Work Session agenda: Board to convene for its work session. This item covers the opening formalities of the meeting, including the welcome, call to order, pledge, and roll call of board members.
Construction begins on Pea Ridge trail. Work was completed Friday on a portion of a trail in Pea Ridge that will eventually cross the city from east to west, connecting trails from Baker-Hayes to It'll Do Road.
Northwest Arkansas ranks high in job and business growth, low in wages. A seven-region study ranked Northwest Arkansas at the top for job growth, business establishment growth, and high-tech employment growth in 2025. The region was at the bottom for average wages, according to the 2026 state of the Northwest Arkansas region report.
Northwest Arkansas commercial real estate market remains tight. The Northwest Arkansas commercial real estate market remained tight in the office, industrial, and retail sectors during the third quarter. This occurred as major projects opened and new development broke ground across the region.
Developer, Benton County, and Rogers collaborate on housing project. The Excellerate Foundation considered locations for its first affordable housing projects when tornadoes in May 2024 devastated parts of eastern Rogers. A developer, Benton County, and Rogers are now working together on a housing project.
Fayetteville school construction project reaches topping-out milestone. The new Woodland Junior High School campus in Fayetteville moved closer to completion with a 'topping out' ceremony. The two-year construction project is slated to open next school year.
Bentonville Public library celebrates 20 years in downtown building. The Bentonville Public Library is marking its 20th anniversary in its downtown building this month.
NWA Council suggests issue 3 could impact local home prices. Proponents of an Arkansas ballot issue argue it could help combat rising housing costs in Northwest Arkansas.
Siloam Springs police cover flock cameras. The city of Siloam Springs has covered all of its license plate readers with black bags. This action follows a vote by the city's board of directors to turn them off.
Aircraft makes emergency landing at XNA. A plane that departed from Northwest Arkansas National Airport on October 23 was forced to circle for over an hour due to a landing gear issue. The plane safely landed back at XNA.
Domino's donates $12,000 to Northwest Arkansas, river valley food banks. Domino's stores across Arkansas collectively donated $12,000 to fight food insecurity on September 15. The donation benefits food banks in Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 23, 2026
item.description:
The Siloam Springs Board of Directors has voted to turn off the city's Flock Safety automated license plate readers.
Siloam Springs board turns off Flock cameras. The Siloam Springs Board of Directors has voted to turn off the city's Flock Safety automated license plate readers for the time being, as the board reviews its contract.
Fayetteville City Council approves 42-acre land purchase for new park. The Fayetteville City Council has approved the purchase of more than 42 acres of land for the development of a new park.
Habitat for Humanity seeks volunteers for Bentonville deconstruction project. Habitat for Humanity Northwest Arkansas is seeking volunteers to help uninstall cabinetry, appliances, and other items from a Bentonville home.
On the Bentonville Schools Board Work Session agenda: Board to convene for a work session. This item marks the formal start of the meeting, including a welcome, call to order, and roll call of board members.
Walmart to launch Agent Profiles for AI shopping. Walmart Inc.'s new Agent Profiles will allow shoppers to use AI agents to shop on their behalf at Walmart and Sam's Club through their apps.
Hope at Christmas seeks Benton County families for holiday assistance. Hope at Christmas 2026 by Sharing and Caring of Benton County is now accepting applications for families in need of assistance with gifts, clothing, bedding, and household essentials this Christmas.
Endeavor Heartland names eight companies for fall accelerator. Bentonville-based Endeavor Heartland recently named eight companies to participate in its fall 2026 ScaleUp Accelerator program, supported by the Walton Family Foundation and the Arkansas Economic Development Commission.
Kwema wins industry security award for Smart Badge. Kwema, a Bentonville-based workplace safety company, recently won the Outstanding New Security Product at the 2026 U.S. Outstanding Security Performance Awards in Atlanta for its Smart Badge.
University of Arkansas launches search for Institute for Integrative and Innovative Research director. The University of Arkansas, Fayetteville, announced it has formed a search committee and hired an outside firm to help select the next director of its Institute for Integrative and Innovative Research.
UnderstandHER summit in Rogers discusses neurodiversity at work. Dress for Success Northwest Arkansas put on a summit in Rogers to bring better understanding to neurodiversity in the workplace.
Fayetteville seeks public input for new park near Owl Creek. The city of Fayetteville is seeking additional public input for a new neighborhood park near Owl Creek as it approaches the final design phase.
Walmart AMP announces 2027 performances. The Walmart AMP is already announcing performances coming to the venue in 2027, with a few concerts remaining on the 2026 docket.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 22, 2026
item.description:
NorthWest Arkansas Community College will host a free fall festival on Thursday, October 22, at its Bentonville campus.
NorthWest Arkansas Community College to host free fall fest. NorthWest Arkansas Community College will host a free fall festival on Thursday, October 22, featuring seasonal activities, food, music, and a family movie night at its Bentonville campus.
NWTI and state office to host industry training luncheon. Northwest Technical Institute (NWTI) in Springdale and the Arkansas Office of Skills Development will jointly host an event on Thursday, October 22, focusing on short-term industry training.
Bentonville animal services to offer fee-waived adoptions. Bentonville Animal Services will offer fee-waived adoptions for the remainder of the calendar year, enabled by a grant.
Benton County Sheriff's Office to host costumes, candy and cops carnival. The Benton County Sheriff's Office will host a free Halloween celebration, the Costumes, Candy and Cops Carnival, which will also serve as an opportunity for a canned food drive.
Springdale shopping center sells for $11.5 million. Three single-story commercial buildings totaling 61,302 square feet in Springdale, anchored by Harps, recently sold for $11.5 million.
NWACC receives $680,000 grant for new trail and amenities. NorthWest Arkansas Community College in Bentonville received a $680,000 grant from the Arkansas Natural and Cultural Resources Council to support the development of a campus bike loop and new recreational amenities.
UAMS opens MS clinic in Fayetteville. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences recently opened the UAMS Health MS Clinic at the UAMS Northwest Regional Campus in Fayetteville.
Lowell and Urban Land Institute seek consultant for downtown plan. The city of Lowell and the Urban Land Institute of Northwest Arkansas are seeking a consultant to assist in developing a downtown master plan for Lowell.
Integrated Openings Solutions opens Little Flock location. Integrated Openings Solutions, a commercial openings systems integrator, recently opened a new location in Little Flock, near Rogers, at 1721 W. Acorn Drive.
Walmart and Sam’s Club combine Plus memberships. Walmart and Sam’s Club are combining their Plus memberships into a single fee of $120 annually or $10 per month, effective October 20.
Walmart to launch AI 'agents' for customer shopping. Walmart is introducing new tools that will allow artificial intelligence (AI) "agents" to shop and complete transactions for customers.
Crystal bridges to debut 'Winter lights' display. Arkansas' largest art museum, Crystal Bridges, will debut an outdoor light exhibit called 'Winter Lights' next month.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 17, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Utility Board and Planning Commission will hold meetings on October 20 to discuss various city matters.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to reallocate $162,800 for unplanned water account expenses. This proposed resolution would move $162,800 from leftover funds from a hydro excavation truck purchase to cover unexpected costs and maintain operations in two water accounts for the rest of the fiscal year.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to amend the 2026 city budget to reallocate $54,164.00. This would shift $54,164.00 of unspent capital funds from the Oldham Road Slope Stabilization Project to the Riordan Road/Highway 71 Improvement Project, affecting which road projects receive funding.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 215 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood transition. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 215 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.2, Neighborhood Transition, potentially allowing for more varied housing types or small-scale commercial uses.
Rogers residents to vote on $457.25 million bond for city projects. Rogers residents will decide on a $457.25 million bond issue to fund improvements for city streets, parks, public safety, and the animal shelter.
Pea Ridge developer seeks variances for collector street. A developer in Pea Ridge has requested numerous street variances from the Planning Commission, which the city attorney stated would "vitiate" city law if granted.
Pea Ridge Planning Commission seeks applicants for two seats. The Pea Ridge Planning Commission is seeking applicants to fill two seats that will expire this year.
Bella Vista seeks public feedback on short-term rental density. The Bella Vista Planning and Development Department is gathering public feedback regarding the density of short-term rental units within the city ahead of a public hearing.
Benton County Quorum Court candidates share reasons for running. Candidates for seven of the 15 seats on the Benton County Quorum Court have shared their reasons for running in the November 3 general election.
America's Car-Mart shares fall 23% after seventh loan extension. Shares of Rogers-based America's Car-Mart fell 23% after the company received its seventh loan extension in six weeks, as it struggles to remain in operation.
Walker park reopens in Fayetteville with new amenities. Walker Park, one of Fayetteville's oldest parks, will reopen this weekend with new athletic facilities and other revamped features.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. Big Sugar Gravel, the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Four Fayetteville centers named america's best ambulatory surgery centers 2027. Newsweek has recognized four Fayetteville surgery centers among the country's best ambulatory surgery centers for 2027.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 16, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will close part of Northeast Chicory Lane starting Friday for multiple days.
Bentonville to close part of northeast chicory lane. The city of Bentonville announced a multi-day road closure for a portion of Northeast Chicory Lane, beginning Friday.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve a contract for engineering services for the 2026 bond-funded radio tower project. This would authorize a contract not to exceed $250,000.00 with Horner & Shifrin for professional engineering services for the construction of a new radio tower.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 501 N Main Street from single-family to neighborhood general. This proposed change would allow for more diverse housing types and potentially more commercial activity at 501 N Main Street, shifting it from a suburban single-family area to a neighborhood general area.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to review minutes from the September 21, 2026 meeting. This is a routine review of past meeting records.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event, which is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Walmart's annual Open Call selects products from 54 entrepreneurs. Walmart's 13th Annual Open Call resulted in 54 entrepreneurs from 35 states and Puerto Rico having their products selected for store shelves and online sales. Nearly 150 entrepreneurs were in Bentonville to promote products made, grown, or assembled in the United States.
J.B. Hunt reports $172.4 million quarterly profit. J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. reported a third-quarter profit of $172.4 million, exceeding analysts' predictions. The company also saw its revenue increase by 20% in the third quarter of 2026.
America's Car-Mart receives seventh loan extension. Rogers-based America's Car-Mart received a seventh extension on some of its loan terms, continuing to work with creditors to maintain operations.
Northwest Arkansas regional planning panel advances highway safety targets. Northwest Arkansas regional planners are considering supporting statewide traffic safety and highway infrastructure targets. This aligns the region's transportation planning with benchmarks set by Arkansas and Missouri transportation officials.
UAMS Schmieding Center to host dementia care conference. The Schmieding Center for Senior Health and Education will host a free conference in Springdale for non-healthcare professionals caring for dementia patients.
Arisa Health CEO Laura Tyler to retire. Dr. Laura Tyler, CEO of Springdale-based behavioral health system Arisa Health, will retire on November 21. Ruth Allison Dover, the chief legal officer, will succeed her as CEO.
Pilgrimage to new beginnings starts in Northwest Arkansas. A three-day pilgrimage, covering over 30 miles from Bentonville to Fayetteville, began on the Razorback Greenway with dozens of participants.
ARDOT awards grants for Northwest Arkansas and river valley projects. The Arkansas Department of Transportation (ARDOT) has awarded grants across two programs to support infrastructure projects in Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley.
Sam's club offers thanksgiving feast deal. Sam's Club is rolling out a Thanksgiving feast deal that can feed 16 people for approximately $160, including a charcuterie board.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 15, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville road closures for infrastructure work have been extended.
Bentonville road closures extended. Two road closures in Bentonville, accommodating infrastructure work, have been extended.
Bentonville city council briefed on Morning Star Schoolhouse renovation. The Bentonville City Council received an update on the ongoing renovation of the Morning Star Schoolhouse. The city anticipates the project will conclude in the spring.
Bentonville Bike Fest moves to September for 2027. The Bentonville Bike Fest will move to September for its 2027 event. Organizers hope the new dates will provide more favorable weather conditions.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event is scheduled for October 17, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale.
J.B. Hunt to release third quarter earnings. J.B. Hunt is scheduled to release the firm’s third quarter earnings.
Crystal bridges symposium to examine Indigenous art legacy. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art will host a symposium on October 16-17. The event will focus on the legacy of Indigenous art.
Silver house community darkroom opens in Springdale. Silver House, a community darkroom for film photographers, has found a home in Springdale. The space will serve as a creative hub for developing pictures and artistic experimentation.
Immerse Arkansas receives $4.5 million for new campus. Immerse Arkansas, a Little Rock-based nonprofit, received a $4.5 million anonymous gift and a 99-year land lease. This funding will establish short-term housing and a campus in Fayetteville.
Fayetteville municipal annex renamed for former mayor. The Fayetteville Municipal Annex has been renamed to honor a former mayor.
Fayetteville to host tenant toolkit event. The City of Fayetteville is inviting renters to a Tenant Toolkit event. The event will provide information on tenant rights, responsibilities, and lease signing.
SoNA Beyond music series begins with 11 concerts. The Symphony of Northwest Arkansas (SoNA) announced its sixth annual SoNA Beyond music series. The series will feature 11 free performances across the region, starting this month.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Council to consider rezoning 501 N Main Street from single-family to neighborhood general. This proposed change would allow for a wider variety of building types beyond single-family homes at 501 N Main Street, potentially increasing density and changing the character of the neighborhood.
On the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Committee agenda: Committee to discuss bylaws for the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Advisory Board. This discussion would review the rules governing the members, terms, attendance, and officer elections for the Tree and Landscape Advisory Board, which could affect how the board operates and makes decisions.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Council to consider proposed amendments to the Bentonville Community Code. These proposed amendments could change the rules and regulations that govern development and land use throughout Bentonville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 14, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville City Council approved a rezoning request for 405 N.W. Fifth St. and accepted a $100,000 grant for library improvements.
Bentonville City Council approves Northwest Fifth street rezoning. The Bentonville City Council approved a second request to rezone 405 N.W. Fifth St., after denying a previous request for the same property last month.
Bentonville Public library to receive $100,000 grant. The Bentonville City Council voted to accept a $100,000 grant from Project for Public Spaces for future library improvement projects.
Rogers City Council accepts $500,000 in infrastructure grants. The Rogers City Council approved the acceptance of over $500,000 in grant funds from the Northwest Arkansas Regional Planning Commission for infrastructure projects.
Bentonville City Council approves land acquisition for infrastructure projects. The Bentonville City Council approved the land acquisition process for three planned road projects, allowing them to progress.
Northwest Arkansas commercial vacancy rates remain low. A new quarterly market summary by Cushman & Wakefield | Sage Partners indicates that the commercial real estate market in Northwest Arkansas, including office, industrial, and retail space, remains tight despite ongoing new construction.
Concerns raised over Northwest Arkansas development and utility coordination. Regional utility providers, planners, and developers have expressed concerns that the pace of development in Northwest Arkansas is outpacing the ability of cities and utility providers to coordinate infrastructure with new projects.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event, which is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Washington regional expands Infusion Center capacity. Washington Regional Medical Center announced the expansion of its Infusion Center at the Fayetteville campus, which will triple its capacity and aim to improve the patient care experience.
Bentonville school bus drivers report fewer 'red-light runners'. Officials note a decrease in violations of school bus safety laws, though some problem areas persist across the Bentonville School District.
Rogers Public library to host lunch and learn on Northwest Arkansas baseball history. Education Manager Ashley Sayers from the Rogers Historical Museum will lead a program focusing on the local history of baseball as part of the Rogers Public Library's Lunch and Learn series.
Matchbox Twenty to perform at Walmart AMP in 2027. Rock band Matchbox Twenty is scheduled to perform at the Walmart AMP as part of the venue's expanding 2027 concert schedule.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 501 N Main Street from single-family to neighborhood general. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and small-scale businesses at 501 N Main Street, rather than only single-family homes.
